--- unit: "C" chapter: "08" lecture: "08a" metadata-files: - ../../_slide-settings.yml format: revealjs: theme: default --- ::: {.my-title} # [Statistical Methods]{.blue} Continuous Moderation ::: {.my-grey} [Unit {{< meta unit >}} | Chapter {{< meta chapter >}}]{}
[Lecture {{< meta lecture >}}]{} ::: ::: {.my-attrib} {{< meta attribution >}} ::: ![](../../img/growth_curve_357EDD.png){.absolute bottom=30 right=0 width="400"} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: # Overview ## Motivation - In the previous chapter, we learned about multiple regression - We used this to predict $y$ from multiple $x$ variables - We accounted for the shared variance among $x$ variables ::: {.fragment} - We will now learn [moderation]{.b .blue} (i.e., interaction effects) - The effect of one $x$ ***depends on*** the value of another $x$ - This adds complexity and "contextualization" to models ::: ## Example dataset Imagine we are doing a study on exercise and energy use ::: {.cell replace_path='["../../data/",""]'} ```{.r .cell-code} #install.packages("marginaleffects") library(tidyverse) exercise <- read_csv("../../data/exercise.csv") exercise ## # A tibble: 900 × 6 ## id expenditure duration intensity sex program ## ## 1 1 18.0 1.84 37.7 male jog ## 2 2 10.2 2.39 26.7 male jog ## 3 3 19.7 2.36 36.3 male jog ## 4 4 1.88 2.52 20.7 male jog ## 5 5 14.2 1.89 24.7 male jog ## 6 6 19.7 2.37 33.7 male jog ## 7 7 11.7 1.95 31.4 male jog ## 8 8 22.0 2.21 39.7 male jog ## 9 9 8.18 2.51 27.6 male jog ## 10 10 5.03 2.17 19.2 male jog ## # ℹ 890 more rows ``` ::: ## Exploratory analysis ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.footer} Note that this is simulated (i.e., fake) data. ::: ## Moderation questions {.fs70} **Continuous-by-Continuous Interaction** - Does the effect of `duration` on `expenditure` depend on `intensity`? ::: {.fragment} **Continuous-by-Categorical Interaction** - Does the effect of `duration` on `expenditure` depend on `sex`? ::: ::: {.fragment} **Categorical-by-Categorical Interaction** - Does the effect of `program` on `expenditure` depend on `sex`? ::: ::: {.fragment} *Note that each question is statistically identical to its reverse (i.e., vice versa).* ::: # Continuous-by-Continuous ## Multiple regression recap Let's regress a continuous $y$ on two continuous $x$ variables $$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2$$ - $b_0$ (intercept): the predicted $y$ when $x_1=0$ and $x_2=0$ - $b_1$ (partial): the change in $y$ for a change of +1 in $x_1$ - $b_2$ (partial): the change in $y$ for a change of +1 in $x_2$ - $b_1$ controls for $x_2$ but is the same across all values of $x_2$ and thus does not depend on it (and the same for $b_2$ and $x_1$) ## Adding an interaction {.fs70} Interactions are formed by multiplying predictor variables The product becomes another predictor with its own slope $$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2 + b_3 \color{red}{x_1 x_2}$$ - $b_0$ (intercept): the predicted $y$ when $x_1=0$ and $x_2=0$ - $b_1$ (simple): the change in $y$ for a change of +1 in $x_1$ (specifically at $x_2=0$) - $b_2$ (simple): the change in $y$ for a change of +1 in $x_2$ (specifically at $x_1=0$) - $b_3$ (interaction): two equivalent definitions + the change in $b_1$ (i.e., the slope of $x_1$) for a change of +1 in $x_2$ + the change in $b_2$ (i.e., the slope of $x_2$) for a change of +1 in $x_1$ ## Rearranging the formula $$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2 + b_3 x_1 x_2$$ ::: {.fragment} $$\hat{y} = b_0 + (b_1 + b_3 x_2) x_1 + b_2 x_2$$ ::: ::: {.fragment} Thus, the slope of $x_1$ (its multiplier) *depends on* the value of $x_2$ Also, if there is no interaction ($b_3=0$), then $b_1$ is unchanged ::: ::: {.fragment .pv2} The same is true for the slope of $x_2$ if we rearrange again $$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + (b_2 + b_3 x_1) x_2$$ ::: ## Interaction and simple effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- lm(expenditure ~ duration + intensity + duration:intensity, data = exercise) model_parameters(fit) ## Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(896) | p ## ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## (Intercept) | 7.80 | 11.60 | [-14.97, 30.57] | 0.67 | 0.502 ## duration | -9.38 | 5.66 | [-20.49, 1.74] | -1.66 | 0.098 ## intensity | -0.08 | 0.38 | [ -0.84, 0.67] | -0.21 | 0.835 ## duration × intensity | 0.39 | 0.19 | [ 0.03, 0.76] | 2.10 | 0.036 ``` ::: - The interaction effect (duration $\times$ intensity) is significant - Thus, the effect of `duration` does depend on `intensity` ::: {.footer} We can also use the shortcut `duration * intensity` ::: ## Predicting energy expenditure {.fs70} $$\hat{y} = 7.80 - 9.38 x_1 - 0.08 x_2 + 0.39 x_1 x_2$$ - **Intercept:** A participant exercising at 0 duration and 0 intensity expends 7.8 units - **Duration Simple Effect:** Each unit of duration will expend an additional -9.38 units of energy (at 0 intensity) - **Intensity Simple Effect:** Each unit of intensity will expend an additional -0.08 units of energy (at 0 duration) - **Interaction Effect:** The slope of duration will increase by 0.39 for each unit of intensity, and the slope of intensity will increase by 0.39 for each unit of duration ::: {.fragment} The average participant (2 duration, 30 intensity) expends 10.04 units of energy $$\hat{y} = 7.80 - 9.38(2) - 0.08(30) + 0.39(2)(30) = 10.04$$ ::: ## Spotlight analysis {.fs70} - In order to plot the predictions, we can map one predictor to the $x$-axis - But representing the other predictor continuously is challenging in 2D ::: {.fragment} - Instead of trying to use a 3D plot, we usually "spotlight" a few values, e.g., + One SD below the mean $(\bar{x} - s_x)$ + The mean value $(\bar{x})$ + One SD above the mean $(\bar{x} + s_x)$ ::: ::: {.fragment} - We plot the effect of one $x$ on $y$ conditional on these values of the other $x$ + Thus, these are often called "conditional effects plots" + You can think of "conditional on" as "depending on" ::: ## Plotting interaction effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(modelbased) plot(estimate_relation(fit, by = c("duration", "intensity=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.footer} The `=[sd]` shortcut spotlights intensity at Mean $\pm$ SD. The lines aren't parallel, so the interaction is non-zero. ::: ## Plotting interaction effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(estimate_relation(fit, by = c("intensity", "duration=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.footer} You can tell there is a non-zero interaction because the lines aren't parallel. ::: ## Simple slopes ::: {.fs70} - What is the slope of `duration` at different values of `intensity`? + With a non-zero interaction, the simple slopes will differ ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} estimate_slopes(fit, trend = "duration", by = "intensity=c(0,15,30,45,60)") ## Estimated Marginal Effects ## ## intensity | Slope | SE | 95% CI | t(896) | p ## ----------------------------------------------------------- ## 0 | -9.38 | 5.66 | [-20.49, 1.74] | -1.66 | 0.098 ## 15 | -3.48 | 2.92 | [ -9.21, 2.26] | -1.19 | 0.235 ## 30 | 2.42 | 0.92 | [ 0.63, 4.22] | 2.65 | 0.008 ## 45 | 8.32 | 2.99 | [ 2.46, 14.19] | 2.78 | 0.005 ## 60 | 14.23 | 5.73 | [ 2.98, 25.47] | 2.48 | 0.013 ## ## Marginal effects estimated for duration ## Type of slope was dY/dX ``` ::: ::: {.footer} We could also use the shortcut `"intensity=[sd]"` to specify Mean $\pm$ SD ::: ## Contrast with No Interaction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit2 <- lm(expenditure ~ duration + intensity, data = exercise) model_parameters(fit2) ## Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(897) | p ## -------------------------------------------------------------------- ## (Intercept) | -15.60 | 3.20 | [-21.88, -9.32] | -4.87 | < .001 ## duration | 2.35 | 0.92 | [ 0.55, 4.15] | 2.56 | 0.010 ## intensity | 0.71 | 0.09 | [ 0.53, 0.88] | 8.00 | < .001 ``` ::: ::: {.fs70} - A participant exercising at 0 duration and 0 intensity expends -15.6 units - Each additional unit of duration will expend 2.35 units (controlling `intensity`) - Each additional unit of intensity will expend 0.71 units (controlling `duration`) - The model predicts the same effect of duration at all values of intensity - The model predicts the same effect of intensity at all values of duration ::: ## Plotting partial effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(estimate_relation(fit2, by = c("duration", "intensity=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.footer} You can tell there is no interaction because the lines are parallel. ::: ## Plotting partial effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(estimate_relation(fit2, by = c("intensity", "duration=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.footer} You can tell there is no interaction because the lines are parallel. ::: ## Simple slopes - In a model with no interaction, all simple slopes are equal ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} estimate_slopes(fit2, trend = "duration", by = "intensity=[sd]") ## Estimated Marginal Effects ## ## intensity | Slope | SE | 95% CI | t(897) | p ## -------------------------------------------------------- ## 24.52 | 2.35 | 0.92 | [0.55, 4.15] | 2.56 | 0.010 ## 29.66 | 2.35 | 0.92 | [0.55, 4.15] | 2.56 | 0.010 ## 34.80 | 2.35 | 0.92 | [0.55, 4.15] | 2.56 | 0.010 ## ## Marginal effects estimated for duration ## Type of slope was dY/dX ``` ::: # Interaction Patterns ## CxC Patterns ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%" .tc .fs70} **Potentiation** As one $x$ increases, the slope of the other increases ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=288} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%" .tc .fs70} **Attenuation** As one $x$ increases, the slope of the other decreases ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=288} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%" .tc .fs70} **Crossover** As one $x$ increases, the ranking of the other reverses ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=288} ::: ::: ::: ::: # Centering with Interactions ## Centering interactions - Recall that the simple effects are when the other $x=0$ + This means that their $p$ values only apply in that region - So, if $x=0$ isn't meaningful, we can use centering + Now they are the slopes when the other $x=\bar{x}$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exercise$duration_c <- center(exercise$duration) exercise$intensity_c <- center(exercise$intensity) ``` ::: ## Centering interactions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit3 <- lm(expenditure ~ duration_c * intensity_c, data = exercise) model_parameters(fit3) ## Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(896) | p ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## (Intercept) | 10.00 | 0.45 | [9.12, 10.89] | 22.13 | < .001 ## duration c | 2.29 | 0.92 | [0.49, 4.09] | 2.50 | 0.012 ## intensity c | 0.71 | 0.09 | [0.53, 0.88] | 8.04 | < .001 ## duration c × intensity c | 0.39 | 0.19 | [0.03, 0.76] | 2.10 | 0.036 ``` ::: ::: {.fs70} - A participant with average duration and intensity expends 10.00 units - Each added unit of duration expends 2.29 units of energy (at average intensity) - Each added unit of intensity expends 0.71 units of energy (at average duration) - The slope of duration will increase by 0.39 for each unit of intensity, and the slope of intensity will increase by 0.39 for each unit of duration ::: ## Plotting centered interactions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(estimate_relation(fit3, by = c("duration_c", "intensity_c=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Plotting centered interactions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(estimate_relation(fit3, by = c("intensity_c", "duration_c=[sd]"))) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](a_Slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Standardizing coefficients - Don't forget that standardizing includes centering! ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_parameters(fit, standardize = "refit") ## Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(896) | p ## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## (Intercept) | -1.15e-03 | 0.03 | [-0.06, 0.06] | -0.04 | 0.971 ## duration | 0.08 | 0.03 | [ 0.02, 0.14] | 2.50 | 0.012 ## intensity | 0.26 | 0.03 | [ 0.20, 0.32] | 8.04 | < .001 ## duration × intensity | 0.07 | 0.03 | [ 0.00, 0.14] | 2.10 | 0.036 ``` ::: ::: {.fs70} - Increasing duration by 1 SD expends another 0.08 SD (at *average* intensity) - Increasing intensity by 1 SD expends another 0.26 SD (at *average* duration) - Increasing duration by 1 SD increases the effect of intensity by 0.07 SDs and
increasing intensity by 1 SD increases the effect of duration by 0.07 SDs ::: ## Recommendations - Center your interacting continuous predictors - Use domain knowledge to guide selection of interactions - Plot your interaction effects to aid in communication - Don't include an interaction without its simple effects - Don't confuse simple effects and partial effects

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
